issue_context.title: LazyFrame ColumnNotFound when casting to a new column
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
from datetime import date, datetime

dt = datetime(2020,1,31,8,31)
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1,2,3], "b": [dt, dt, dt]})
df_lazy = df.lazy().with_columns(pl.col("b").cast(pl.Datetime).alias("c"))
df_lazy_no_cast = df.lazy().with_columns(pl.col("b").alias("c"))

def bad_filter(lazy_df: pl.LazyFrame) -> pl.LazyFrame:
    return lazy_df.filter(
        pl.col('c').dt.date() == pl.lit(date(2020,1,31))
    ).filter(
        (pl.col('c').dt.date() >= pl.lit(date(2020,1,31))) &
        (pl.col('c').dt.datetime() < pl.lit(datetime(2020,1,31,10,31)))
    )

# this errors
bad_filter(df_lazy).collect()

# this succeeds
bad_filter(df_lazy.collect().lazy()).collect()

# this also succeeds
bad_filter(df_lazy_no_cast).collect()
```


### Log output

```shell
File "polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 1787, in collect
    return wrap_df(ldf.collect())
polars.exceptions.ColumnNotFoundError: c
```


### Issue description

Subsequent filters on LazyFrame do not recognize column `c`, which has been constructed as `pl.col('b').cast(pl.Datetime).alias('c')`.

Notably, removing this `cast` results in the expected behavior. Additionally, running `.collect().lazy()` before filtering also fixes the problem.

### Expected behavior

The output should be this:

```
>> bad_filter(df_lazy.collect().lazy()).collect()
shape: (3, 3)
┌─────┬─────────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│ a   ┆ b                   ┆ c                   │
│ --- ┆ ---                 ┆ ---                 │
│ i64 ┆ datetime[μs]        ┆ datetime[μs]        │
╞═════╪═════════════════════╪═════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 │
│ 2   ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 │
│ 3   ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 ┆ 2020-01-31 08:31:00 │
└─────┴─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
```

### Installed versions

<details>

Was able to reproduce this on both my linux machine running latest polars, as well as my legacy Mac machine using polars-lts-cpu.

```
--------Version info---------
Polars:              0.19.9
Index type:          UInt32
Platform:            macOS-10.16-x86_64-i386-64bit
Python:              3.9.18 (main, Sep 11 2023, 08:38:23) 
[Clang 14.0.6 ]
```

</details>
comments:
This is caused by `predicate push down`, and can be reproduced by more simpler example:

```python
   df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
    out = (
        df.lazy()
        .select(pl.col("a").cast(pl.Int64).alias("b"))
        .filter(pl.col("b") == 1)
        .filter((pl.col("b") >= 1) & (pl.col("b") < 1))
    )
    out.explain(predicate_pushdown=True)
```

```python
FILTER [(col("b")) == (1)] FROM
 SELECT [col("a").strict_cast(Int64).alias("b")] FROM
  DF ["a"]; PROJECT 1/1 COLUMNS; SELECTION: "[([(col(\"b\")) >= (1)]) & ([(col(\"b\")) < (1)])]"
```

`col("b")`  was somehow pushed down into `DF`.  Let me see how to fix it.
